title: Today's Work, Tomorrow's Workforce: Incentivizing Learning in AI-Assisted Work
abstract: arXiv:2611.06346v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: At work, people develop skills through experience: novices acquire skills by completing tasks, while experts retain theirs through continued practice. AI assistance changes this process by offering workers a choice between solving tasks independently and accepting the AI's answers. While relying on AI saves immediate effort, it can also displace the practice needed to acquire and retain skills, including those required to oversee the AI. We extend an existing accept-or-solve model to a sequence of tasks in which workers' skills evolve through independent practice and reliance on AI. We compare myopic workers, who maximize immediate utility, with strategic workers, who also value their future skills. We show that novices can become trapped at low skill levels, while experts may lose skill, even as AI-assisted outcome accuracy remains high. translated_title: 今日之工作，明日之劳动力：激励AI辅助工作中的学习
translated_abstract: 在工作中，人们通过经验积累技能：新手通过完成任务习得技能，而专家则通过持续练习保持技能。AI辅助改变了这一过程，为工作者提供了独立解决任务或接受AI答案的选择。虽然依赖AI能节省眼前的精力，但它也可能取代获得并保持技能所需的练习，其中包括监督AI所需的技能。我们将现有的“接受或解决”模型扩展到一个任务序列中，其中工作者的技能通过独立练习和对AI的依赖而不断演变。我们比较了最大化即时效用的短视工作者与同时重视未来技能的策略性工作者。我们证明，即使AI辅助下的结果准确率依然很高，新手也可能被困在低技能水平，而专家可能丧失技能。相比之下，策略性工作者即使在AI更准确的情况下也可能选择独立解决问题……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究表明，依赖AI辅助会侵蚀技能积累——新手可能陷入低技能陷阱、专家可能技能退化，而重视未来技能的策略性工作者即使AI更准确也会选择独立解题以维持练习。
en_tdlr: Reliance on AI assistance can trap novices at low skill levels and cause experts' skills to decay, while strategic workers who value their future skills may choose to solve tasks independently even when AI is more accurate.
